gravity.source: WGS84 normal gravity (Somigliana formula, NIMA TR8350.2, 2000) with the TR8350.2 height series, at the two worst cases: the highest town (La Rinconada, Peru, 5,100 m, Guinness World Records) put at the equator gives 9.7646; the lowest land (the Dead Sea shore, about 430 m below sea level, Britannica) put at a pole gives 9.8335. Rounded outward to two decimals. Weaknesses: constants and heights were read only as web-search excerpts, no page could be opened from our network; TR8350.2 itself was not opened; the series constant m is from memory. Working in research/34-planet-ranges.md.

airDensity.source: Dry air, ideal gas, ISO 2533 standard atmosphere. Densest: the record sea-level pressure 1083.8 hPa (Agata, Siberia, 1968) with the record low-station cold -67.8 °C (Verkhoyansk, 1892) gives 1.8386. Thinnest: standard pressure at the highest town (5,100 m, 53,302 Pa) with the hottest temperature ever recorded, 56.7 °C (Death Valley, 1913, WMO archive) gives 0.5629. Rounded outward to two decimals. Weaknesses: each end joins extremes that never happen together, so the range is wide on purpose; dry air; all figures were read only as web-search excerpts, no page could be opened from our network; how far real pressure at 5,100 m falls below standard was not found. Working in research/34-planet-ranges.md.
